chunk_findings.detail: The path detector counts any `word/word` token in prose as a named file, so text that names no file at all is treated as "text that names files", and every source glob is dropped instead of inherited. `_PATHISH`'s first alternative `[\w.*-]+(?:/[\w.*-]+)+` does not require the token to look like a path, only that its segments are word chars, so ordinary slash-joined prose matches: `"and/or"`, `"read/write"`, `"client/server"`, `"24/7"`, `"w/o"`, `"C/C++"` (matches `"C/C"`), and URLs (`"github.com/foo/bar.py"`). Concretely, with the source item's globs `["ddflow/services/merge.py"]` and a bug summary `"the read/write path races"`, `inherit_globs` returns `[]`: for the single named token `read/write`, all four tests in `_names` are false (`fnmatch("read/write","ddflow/services/merge.py")` false, no suffix match, and `fnmatch("write","merge.py")` false), so the comprehension yields nothing. This directly contradicts the function's own documented contract ("Text naming no file inherits them all") and the fix's purpose: for a bug summary phrased with a slash-word, the fix task silently inherits none of the globs of the item it was found in — the opposite failure mode of B76f42d8f1f. The added tests only exercise prose with no slash (`"the parser drops a line"`), so this case is untested.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bug_globs.py:23-24 (_PATHISH / inherit_globs)

chunk_findings.detail: `_PATHISH` only recognizes a token as a file when it contains a `/` or ends in one of `_EXTS`. A bug summary that names a single-segment file without one of those extensions — e.g. `"merge is slow; see Dockerfile"`, `"check uv.lock"`, `"the LICENSE changed"` — yields `named == []`, so `inherit_globs` takes the "naming no file" branch and returns every source glob, including the unrelated ones this change is meant to strip. With source globs `["ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py", "ddflow/services/bug_globs.py", "tests/test_claim.py"]` and summary `"merge is slow; see Dockerfile"`, the result is the full list rather than `[]`, i.e. fix-B76f42d8f1f's symptom (fix task carrying `claim.py` etc. for a merge bug) still occurs for this class of input. Whether this matters depends on how often such summaries occur, hence LOW.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `_PATHISH` still matches ordinary prose, just a narrower subset: the first alternative requires a `/`-joined token whose *last* segment contains a `.` or `*`, so any slash-word at the end of a sentence matches because the sentence's full stop is the required dot. `re.findall` on a summary like `"the split is 50/50."` yields `["50/50."]`, `"runs 24/7."` yields `["24/7."]`, and `"the flag is either/or."` yields `["either/or."]`. `_names` then compares that junk token against the source globs (`fnmatch("50/50.", "ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py")` etc., all false), so `inherit_globs` hits the `if not named` false branch and returns `[]` — the exact opposite of the documented contract "Text naming no file inherits them all", and the fix task loses every glob even though the bug names nothing. The regression test `test_slash_words_in_prose_are_not_file_names` only exercises the no-punctuation forms (`"the read/write path races"`, `"and/or 24/7 client/server"`, `"w/o a lease"`), so it passes while the trailing-period cases the previous review raised are still live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bug_globs.py:25 (`_PATHISH`, `inherit_globs`)

chunk_findings.detail: A summary that names a single-segment file whose name is not in `_EXTS` is invisible to the heuristic: `"merge is slow; see Dockerfile"`, `"check uv.lock"`, `"the LICENSE changed"`, `"Makefile"` produce `named == []` (no slash, no `.py|md|toml|...` suffix), so `inherit_globs` takes the "naming no file" branch and returns *every* source glob, including the unrelated `claim.py` this change exists to strip. Concretely, with `source_globs=["ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py", "ddflow/services/bug_globs.py"]` and `text="merge is slow; see Dockerfile"`, the function returns both globs instead of `[]`, because the file the text actually names never enters `named`. The test suite (`test_text_naming_only_other_files_inherits_nothing`) uses `README.md`, an extension that happens to be listed, so it does not cover this.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite only narrowed the *slash* alternative of `_PATHISH`; the bare-name alternative is still `[\w-]+\.(?:{_EXTS})\b` with the closed list `py|md|toml|json|ya?ml|sh|txt|cfg|ini|js|ts|rs|go|c|h`. Any summary that names a file by a name with no dot (extension-less) or with an extension outside that list is therefore invisible to the heuristic, `_PATHISH.findall(text)` returns `[]`, and `inherit_globs` takes the "text naming no file" branch and returns *every* source glob — the exact behaviour this change exists to remove. Concrete input: `source_globs = ["ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py", "ddflow/services/bug_globs.py", "tests/test_claim.py"]` with `summary = "merge timed out; see Dockerfile"` (same for `"check uv.lock"`, `"the LICENSE changed"`, `"Makefile"`, or off-list extensions such as `"the template is index.html"`, `"schema.sql changed"`, `"style.css"` — html/sql/css/xml/lock are not in `_EXTS`). `_PATHISH` matches nothing in these strings (no `/` for the first alternative, and the second alternative needs `\.(py|md|…)`), so `named == []` and the fix task is again handed `claim.py`. This is the earlier reported gap (the one whose triage is still `untriaged`), and it still holds: the diff's regex change does not touch `_EXTS` and adds no fallback for a token that has no recognised extension, so nothing in the new code answers it.

chunk_findings.detail: The function only narrows the glob list when the bug text contains a recognizable filename token; when it does not, it returns the source item's full glob list unchanged. That is exactly the input of the bug this change claims to fix: B76f42d8f1f's own subject is `ddflow merge timeout`, which names no file. Given the source globs quoted in the intent (`... claim.py, services/completion.py, tests/test_claim_bug_globs.py ...`) and `inherit_globs(SRC, "ddflow merge timeout")`, `_PATHISH.findall` returns `[]`, the `if not named: return list(source_globs)` branch is taken, and the fix task is still created with `claim.py` and the other unrelated globs — the exact failure the bug reports. The supplied regression test passes only because it injects a decoy filename (`"merge timed out; README.md stale"`) that forces the filtering branch; no test exercises the real summary. So the change does not fix the reported bug for its own reproduction input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bug_globs.py:33 (`inherit_globs` fallback)

chunk_findings.detail: The basename clause retains a source glob whenever the *basename* of a named file equals the basename of the glob, regardless of directory, which contradicts the docstring ("keeps only the source globs it names … none, when it names others") and re-creates the very bug being fixed. Concrete input: `inherit_globs(["ddflow/services/config.py"], "scripts/config.py mistimes the lease")` returns `["ddflow/services/config.py"]`, even though the text names no source file — the first three clauses all fail and the final `fnmatch("config.py", "config.py")` succeeds. Same thing happens for common duplicated basenames (`__init__.py`, `utils.py`, `models.py`): a bug text naming `pkgA/utils.py` silently keeps `pkgB/utils.py`, i.e. an unrelated glob is written onto the fix task. The four clauses the tests cover (bare basename, suffix path, wildcard) are already handled by clauses 1–3, so this final clause only adds false positives.

chunk_findings.detail: The narrowing only happens when `_PATHISH` finds a filename token in the text. The bug this change exists to close, B76f42d8f1f, is described by the text `ddflow merge timeout`, which names no file, so `inherit_globs(["core/records.py", "handlers/knowledge.py", "api/knowledge/bugs.py", "services/completion.py", "claim.py", "tests/test_claim_bug_globs.py"], "ddflow merge timeout")` hits the `if not named` branch and returns that same full list unchanged. That is precisely the symptom in the bug report: the fix task for the merge-timeout bug is again handed `core/records.py`, `claim.py`, `tests/test_claim_bug_globs.py`, etc., none of which the bug is about. The refutation's probe does not answer this: `test_bug_found_does_not_copy_unrelated_globs` (per the triage) uses a text that names `README.md`, a different input from the bug's own summary, and the `test_bugs_as_items` inheritance tests only pin the unnamed-text fallback — together they show a *narrowed* case works and that inherit-all is a contract, but not that the motivating case (`summary` = "ddflow merge timeout") stops inheriting the unrelated globs it complains about. So the reported input still reproduces on the fixed code.
